title: Routed experts on the CPU tier in the device's declared order
description: host-expert-tier's contract. Host form: routes grouped by expert in route order, at most max_tokens a chunk, each route's unweighted output row in FP32, then device_sum multiplies by the routing weight and sums a token's routes in plan order with one FP32 rounding per operation (within FP32 rounding of the reference). Device form on the CPU: nvfp4 (W4A4) and int4 (W4A8) experts as bundles read in place, each route's row in host-expert-arithmetic's declared integer block order (the bits of a device kernel that declares it), summed in route order by FMAs; the native tier (C++ over a pinned worker pool, built at load) or the same order in torch where it does not build.

max_tokens.description: host form: routes of one expert in a chunk

native.description: the device form's rows: the native tier built at load (on: refuse to load without it), or the declared order in torch (off), the same bits; auto takes the native tier where it builds

workers.description: the native tier's worker threads (-1: one per physical core but the caller's)

pin.description: pin each worker to a physical core of its own (Linux)

spin_us.description: the least an idle CPU worker spins before it sleeps

rows_per_task.description: rows of one expert in a pool task

spin_max_us.description: an idle CPU worker spins as long as the recent gaps between batches (1.5 times the longest of the last 16), at most this, then sleeps: awake through a decode step's layers, asleep between steps (0: spin_us only). The default was measured on one machine (6 cores, WSL2, decode layers about 1.2 ms apart): measure your own cadence
